“I’ve been… unwell.”

Mydei interrupted the excited squeaks gathering around them, his voice quiet and unsure as they sat down in an isolated corner within the Garden of Life. A hoard of chimaeras, giddy at the prospect of evading their jobs to come and play with their beloved ‘Wonderful Amazing Cool Chimaera King Dei’ and ‘Miss Hyacine’, immediately began clambering all over the two, chirping and wiggling with glee.

Hyacine shuddered when tiny claws dug into her leg, a worthy sacrifice that resulted in a familiar ginger chimaera settling in her lap. Then Mydei's words registered, and she looked at him. “What?”

Her distraction elicited an unhappy little ‘awoo’ to spring from the chimaera using her as a throne, so she twiddled her fingers through its soft fur and cooed as it rolled over to show her its soft white tummy.

The two Chrysos heirs were relaxing in the Garden of Life – though if you asked Mydei, he would suggest that they were fulfilling an important mission to help boost workers’ morale – and trying to appear useful instead of merely lazing around like plump unicorns.

Ever since the departure of the Trailblazers and the end to those long, stressful months in which the progress of the Flamechase was suddenly hastened to a fantastic conclusion, Hyacine had found herself surprisingly short of work to do.

It wasn’t as if Amphoreus was completely restored to its former glory and all the threats of rogue titankin were eradicated. It wasn’t even as if Hyacine and the other Chrysos heirs had lost the golden blood that granted them enhanced ability. No, the only change was that without the black tide flowing rampant, the city was plunged into a liminal state of peace.

So here they were, playing with chimaeras and pretending that they were doing profound work.

Mydei was frowning while patting a cute little chimaera pup; its father snoozed against his thigh, eerily similar to the one that had nipped Hyacine months ago. Hyacine had to admit, he made an adorable sight, trying to look all serious and muscular while cradling a pup like his baby.

“I mean to say, I think there is something awry within me.” He placed stress on the end of his sentence, looking at Hyacine expectantly as if she were supposed to be a mind reader alongside a healer. She could only wish.

Hyacine gently lifted the ginger chimaera from her lap, placing it on the ground to let it waddle over to Mydei and cuddle up to the white chimaera on his thigh. “What do you mean by that? With your immortal body, I thought…” Aquila above, she was starting to sound like Phainon, always harping on about Mydei’s body.

Golden eyes were focused on the two chimaeras nestled against him, slowly shifting to the pup in his arms.

“This one… is theirs?”

“Um, probably? That white chimaera is its father; it’s particularly vicious if you try to separate them.”

Mydei nodded, understanding and something else lighting up in his eyes as he watched the pup with a tender gaze. Then he cleared his throat, beckoned Hyacine closer, and leaned in to speak. “My body protects me from most diseases, it’s true, but lately, I’ve been feeling strange.” He raised a hand to fiddle with his braid. “I’ve been drowsier than usual, and somewhat nauseous.”

The fatigue shouldn’t have been a major cause of concern, seeing as Mydei was already prone to taking frequent naps during the day. Hyacine could easily recall at least twenty-seven instances in which a civilian had stumbled across the slumbering man, accidentally awoken him, and come begging to Hyacine to grant them protection from the ‘enraged lion’.

Though anyone could tell that Mydei was less of an ‘enraged lion’ when stirred from his naps, but rather, a ‘confused kitten’. Phainon’s words, not Hyacine’s. He had once spent an entire Lucid hour regaling his favourite positions, locations and outfits that he had caught Mydei napping in around Okhema. Hm, no, actually, Hyacine didn’t want to remember that.

Moving on. Mydei’s nausea, however, could be a problem – it was usually a sign of internal imbalance and could suggest something was wrong, not to mention the risk of malnutrition from a suppressed appetite. For a man as reliant on his physical state as Mydei, frequent nausea was certain to be a curse.

Yet strangely enough, despite nausea often inhibiting hunger, Mydei had been displaying a completely different effect. From what Hyacine had seen of Mydei their last few encounters, stolen glimpses of the prince tucked away in a corner with a platter of sweets in hand, or greeting him at the baths while Phainon was feeding him grapes as though he were a spoiled housecat, a common denominator remained – the snacking.

An annoying little voice in her head, suspiciously reminiscent of a familiar white haired man, whispered, Mydei's obviously showing symptoms of pregnancy. He's done it, Phainon's defied biology, he's put a baby in him.

Hyacine smacked her palm to her head. Ha, what a thought.

Ignoring Mydei's confused face, his jaw dropped at her reaction, Hyacine rushed to say, “But you’ve been snacking a lot more, haven’t you? It can’t just be a regular disease, seeing as the nausea hasn't inhibited your appetite, but made it bigger.”

“So you agree then,” Mydei said, and a radiant grin erupted on his face as though Hyacine had just shared brilliant news. “It is something within my body.”

“Perhaps you’ve been working too hard? Cassie mentioned that you keep taking missions, even though there’s really no need…”

To be honest, it wasn't that there was a lack of need for Mydei's help – he was invaluable in clearing up the leftover corrupted titankin, as well as leading Okhema's expeditionary forces into the newly cleansed land. Rather, Mydei's dedication to rebuilding and repopulating the fallen Amphorean cities seemed to border on obsession.

Mydei frowned, his hands balling on the ground beside him. “Only because Phainon never lets me do anything. He treats me like a princess locked in a tower, always trying to do everything before I even lift a finger.” He started tugging at the grass, repeatedly plucking and dropping it on the white chimaera’s back. “I mean, he doesn't even want me cleaning up around the house anymore.”

That didn’t sound so bad to Hyacine. It was like complaining that the grass was too green, the sky was too blue, the chimaeras too cute. She would love to have someone helping her with her chores, clearing up messes and sorting out her neverending to-do lists without a word. Instead she had Ica.

“He says he ‘needs to pamper his wife’, but I’m so bored. And now I’m sick.”

Phainon was probably still in the honeymoon phase, eager to please Mydei and prove himself to be a worthy match. Hyacine could remember that was exactly how he had behaved during their first year at the Grove, all polite and friendly like an obedient puppy, even if their professor asked him to do the most mundane tasks.

She could imagine the man flitting around their house with a broom in hand, happily sweeping the floors and wiping the counters and doing the laundry. Her eyes focused on the white chimaera, its eyes half-open as it let Mydei unconsciously cover it in grass.

“Just yesterday, he tried cooking dinner.”

Scratch that, it wasn’t a honeymoon phase, Phainon was trying to kill Mydei.

“Could it be food poisoning?” Hyacine had firsthand experience with the man’s cuisine, and she had had to prepare an antidote for it immediately afterwards. “I hate to say it, but Phainon’s cooking isn’t exactly–”

“His cooking’s abysmal, even red soil tastes better than his bread,” Mydei said, waving a hand in dismissal as if that would conceal the dromas in the room.

“Mydei,” Hyacine began slowly, “Mydei, have you been eating dromas feed?”

Even Ica didn’t touch that.

“That’s not the point, I’ve been feeling off for longer than his weird protectiveness has started.” There was a slight flush to Mydei’s cheeks as he tapped his chin in thought. “Maybe about a month or so.”

A month?! By Aquila, Hyacine needed to step up her game if her patients were waiting a month to tell her of their sickness.

She was about to speak, her physician’s persona switching on in preparation for a full breakdown of Mydei’s symptoms, when a pair of hands covered his golden eyes.

“Guess who!”

Hyacine’s day could not get any worse.

Mydei chuckled and pulled one of the hands down to plant a gentle kiss to the palm. Then he leaned back, golden eyes meeting blue as he gave Phainon a disgustingly tender look. Hyacine’s day got worse.

It wasn’t even as if she hated their relationship; on the contrary, she appreciated their love. Sure, she wasn’t a diehard fan of the two men like Castorice, nor a general supporter of romance like Aglaea, but she could appreciate the beauty and strength of the bond they shared.

It’s just, she would prefer if they didn’t display that bond so blatantly in front of her.

And clearly, she had a supporter in this belief.

The white chimaera, previously seated so peacefully beside Mydei, crouched on its haunches, leaped up with an enraged ‘awoo’ and snapped at Phainon’s shin, eliciting a shrill yelp as the man toppled over. Hyacine blinked. She didn’t think even her voice could reach that pitch.

Then, while Phainon lay in a heap on the ground, the chimaera stood on its hind legs to pluck its white-haired baby from Mydei’s arms, securing the pup in its mouth to deposit it under the ginger chimaera’s paw and huddle together once more.

Mydei only watched the exchange with an amused silence, waiting for the chimaera family to settle down before turning to pull his unruly husband up off the floor.

Like a petulant child, Phainon was pouting, and he sniffed dramatically as he rested his chin on Mydei’s bare shoulder. “Mydeiii,” he whined, “I got attacked.”

He was a grown man.

Phainon, a formidable warrior capable of battling with Titans and scratching cosmic entities from even outside the boundaries of Amphoreus’ existence, was acting like a child over a little nip from a chimaera.

“Don't be a baby, Deliverer.” Mydei chided, but he still turned his head to press a soft kiss to Phainon's cheek and tangled his fingers in snowy hair.

Hyacine's face twisted in disgust, outraged at the sickeningly sweet display of affection she was being forced to witness. Though unfortunately, the others were too lost in each other’s presence to notice her metaphorical foaming at the mouth.

“What's it gonna take for you to give me a more loveable nickname?” Came a mournful sigh as Phainon wrapped his arms around Mydei's waist to settle his palms on his stomach. Hyacine noticed the blond perk up slightly at that. “Maybe ‘honey’, or ‘sweetheart’, or ‘darling’… hey, you call me ‘husband’ so sweetly when we–”

She actually didn't want to hear that. It was honestly baffling how it seemed that they would save their most sappy conversations for when she was around, like they were taking every chance they could go make her feel wildly out of place.

In the centre of their little gathering, the culprit behind Phainon's attack sat peacefully, having trotted over to Hyacine once the blubbering started. It rolled over and showed her its fluffy white tummy, inviting her to stroke.

Well, she wasn't going to complain.

“I think ‘Deliverer’ is a loveable nickname though? It's for you,” Mydei said, drawing her out of her thoughts, “and I love you.” He spoke frankly, like he was telling Phainon something so obvious he had not expected to have to spell it out.

Hyacine could only watch in horror as Phainon's eyes widened, his cheeks pinked and he leaped forward to knock Mydei over onto the grass with a squeal of, “Oh Mydei!”

“Wha– get off me!”

And then, as if their canoodling wasn't enough, the two men started grappling like children, rolling in the grass and muddying themselves with clear grins stretched across their faces.

Even the chimaera family were wary of the scene, the ginger one lifting up its pup by the scruff and hastily trotting away while the white one guarded its back with suspicion, eyeing the tussling men like some strange, obscene new threat.

Maybe Hyacine should follow their lead.

Hyacine ducked as the titankin swung towards her with a solid mace, her hat flying off of her head and landing on the ground right next to its feet. She eyed it in despair when the titankin lifted its stone foot, about to sully the fabric with its slimy secretions, until a blur of lilac flashed into sight.

Castorice swung her scythe into the titankins midriff and with a burst of flowers, it crumbled into dust and buried the hat under a grey pile. Oh well, dust was easier to clean than slime.

The two Chrysos heirs were a little ways outside Okhema on a mission to clear up the random resurgence of corrupt titankin bothering the farmers. To do so, Tribbie had supplied them with a purification totem, which they had to plant on a suitable point in order to create a safe zone from any further disturbance.

Thankfully, Hyacine had been paired with Castorice, so she didn't have to worry about the fighting. The woman fought with intense vigour and yet remained calm, as if she were merely plucking the petals from a flower – beautiful and deadly.

Even Ica, hurtling into the titankin with strikes of brute force, didn't look as composed.

“Cassie, we make a great pair, huh?” Hyacine called out, her eyes twinkling and bright at the sight of the demigod slicing through titankin like an angel of death. She kept all their attention on her, leaving Hyacine free to plant the totem in the ground.

Except when she heard those words, something strange happened: a wash of pink flooded Castorice’s face.

Wow.

Luckily, she had destroyed most of the titankin surrounding them, for she stood frozen in place, her cheeks adorably flushed and her eyes wide with an unnameable emotion. Hyacine watched with interest as her fingers flexed and unflexed around the handle of her scythe, her lips slightly parted around a sudden intake of breath.

Then there was an enraged screech right next to Hyacine’s ear – a titankin had snuck up on her, pot-bellied and roaring with fury, its hand drawn back and poised to strike with a golden goblet.

Castorice was too far to reach it in time, and Hyacine's eyes squeezed shut as she braced her core to tank the hit; sure, she wasn't Mydei, capable of walking off stab wounds and broken limbs like they were merely insect bites, but she wasn't a Chrysos heir for nothing.

The blow never landed. Instead, all Hyacine heard was a shrill, “Brrrt!”

Her eyes snapped open. Ica, brilliant Ica, had locked in on the opponent and zoomed forward to knock it backwards, creating enough distance for Hyacine to scramble to the side while the tiny unicorn faced off with the titankin.

Castorice gasped out an apology and darted forward, raising her hand and tapping the titankin lightly on the chest to kill it in an instant. Her gaze was narrowed, her normally kind violet eyes filled with a sliver of annoyance.

Woah, Hyacine thought with a smile broadening on her face, Cassie looked quite… cool.

“Ah, Miss Hyacine, watch out!”

It seemed that the titankin was not a normal one – Hyacine should have been able to tell based on its potbelly swinging around and the goblet in its hand. Unfortunately, she hadn’t noticed and, with that dazed grin still plastered on her face, she hadn’t moved out of the line of fire.

There was a grotesque noise as the titankin exploded, its pink slimy innards bursting directly all over Hyacine and covering her in a foul-smelling heap of mush.

Still, Hyacine was a little distracted by the worried expression on Castorice’s face, her arm outstretched as if to try to protect Hyacine from the blast. Oh, she was too cute.

Then a sizeable drop of goop dripped into Hyacine’s eye and she let out a screech.

“Miss Hyacine!” Hasty footsteps rushed towards her, and the telltale feeling of drowsiness that accompanied Castorice’s presence began to take over Hyacine’s body.

Realising her mistake, the footsteps stopped, followed by an upset, “Ah, my apologies!”

“Doot doot!” A familiar plump snout nudged Hyacine’s arm as Ica grabbed her sleeve, tugging her forward.

“Ica, you’ll guide me?”

“Brrt!”

“I think it’s best that we head straight to the baths, Miss Hyacine.” Castorice’s voice was heavy with regret – she was most likely distressed at seeing her covered in titankin slime – but she spoke louder than usual so that she could be heard through the gunk blocking Hyacine’s ears. “I don’t know what sort of titankin that was, but it can’t be safe to have its… secretions all over you.”

Even in the horrid situation she was in, Hyacine felt giddy over the worry in her voice. “Heh, not to worry, Cassie. I think that was just one of Phagousa’s Scions. They’re gross, but harmless.”

Phagousa’s Scions were a derivative of titankin that hailed from Styxia, old drunkards that fought using goblets of slime and exploded into slop once defeated. Professor Anaxa had brought one of them into a lecture once, rambling about experimenting on how to kill them without getting covered in their innards.

Suffice to say,  after that class, the Grove’s communal showers were full.

Hyacine bemoaned her fate. She could remember how intensely she had had to scrub to get the slime off her clothes, though at least it had blended in with her hair – Phainon’s head was stained pink for a whole week.

Thankfully, the walk to the baths wasn’t too long, and Ica made for a surprisingly good guide. Probably because they had a large surface area.

It was fairly late in the day as well; the last Hyacine had checked, it was around the fourth quint of Parting hour, so most citizens would be at home enjoying dinner with their families. The only people on the streets were the vendors packing up and the partygoers getting started on their nightly trysts.

Quietly, Hyacine, Ica and Castorice made their way into the Marmoreal Palace.

“Watch your step, Miss Hyacine. We’re at the lift,” Castorice warned, and Hyacine passed her a grateful smile.

“Thanks, Cassie,” She carefully lifted her foot to climb on, “You know, you don’t have to call me ‘Miss Hyacine’. Makes me feel like one of my stuffy old lecturers. Just Hyacine is fine.”

There was a silence as Castorice got on the lift behind her. And then, in a teasing voice “Oh? But, Lady Tribios gets to call you Cinny.”

If Hyacine could see, and if she wasn’t panicking over the fact that Castorice – sweet, serious Castorice – was teasing her, she might have caught the woman pressing her palms to her face in an attempt to cover the furious blush swarming her delicate features.

But unfortunately, the titans hated her.

Hyacine was about to respond, about to tell her that yes, of course she could call her Cinny, or any nickname she liked, when the sound of voices drifted down from above.

“I wonder who’s up here so late.”

Even Aglaea didn’t tend to bathe this late in the day, spending her evenings placidly sewing and consolidating her orders for the day. Hyacine couldn’t think of a time when she had set foot in the baths at this time, always busy clearing up the medical bay after a day of work.

“...wait,” Castorice said, her voice filled with a subtle excitement. “What time is it?”

“Uh,” It was a good thing teleslates were accessible for the blind, as Hyacine could check the time with just a press of the button on the side. “Fifth quint of Parting hour?”

There was a squeak beside her, but it was quickly covered by a cough.

Ok.

The moving platform stopped in place, finally at the top, but Hyacine had no room for relief when she heard who the mysterious voices belonged to.

“Calm down, Mydei, I just want to cuddle,” Came a familiar voice, followed by a splash of water and the noise of skin-on-skin, as though arms had wrapped around someone in a hug.

“You never just want to cuddle, the last time–” The angry words were cut off by a disgusted gasp, voicing the feeling Hyacine was trying hard to suppress inside.

The sound of water rippling and hitting the edge of the baths drifted to Hyacine’s ears as someone stood up, the gentle patter of feet on the tiles following as they approached.

“Lord Mydei, Lord Phainon.” Castorice greeted.

Phainon’s voice sounded constipated when he said, “Castorice, Hyacine! You guys are back!”

“It's good to see you, Castorice,” Mydei’s voice was closer than she realised, and he took Hyacine’s hand gently as he guided her to the bath in place of Ica. “What in Nikador’s name happened to you, Hyacine?”

When they were in the water, Hyacine stood in place awkwardly as Mydei began rubbing at her face, dedicatedly scrubbing away at the goop and mess left behind by the titankin. Hyacine felt like a baby chimaera being groomed by its mother.

“Um,” She wasn’t about to mention the fact that she had been distracted by Castorice’s blush, “We ran into one of Phagousa’s Scions.”

“Phagousa's Scions? I thought they kept to Styxia. I remember one of Professor Anaxa's lectures on the site fidelity of titankin based on their corresponding Titan,” Phainon called out, and then there was a contemplative silence before he continued. “D’you think maybe they're migrating?”

Hyacine wasn’t really in the mood to think. Mydei’s hands were firm but gentle, and she was feeling sleepy under his ministrations as he washed her. Though, perhaps that was an important thing to think about, seeing as abnormal titankin could cause more harm then good.

There was a rinse of water over her face, and then finally, finally, Hyacine could see again!

She wished she couldn’t. Upon opening her eyes, she was immediately faced with the view of Mydei’s focused gaze as he directed his attention to cleaning her hair, and over Mydei’s shoulder, Phainon’s loving eyes staring dreamily at the blond’s face.

The whole bath was empty, and Phainon just had to stand plastered to Mydei like a limpet.

Hyacine wanted to look away from the men in front of her, only to catch sight of fabric slipping off of pale skin as Castorice undressed. Yeah, no, she would have to look at the floor.

But the floor was no better, as on the pile of discarded clothes was her hat, slightly dusty, but in good condition. Hyacine had to hold back a squeal – Castorice had picked it up for her and carried it safely all the way.

Then she remembered Phainon had asked a question, and hastily responded, “I guess, maybe. Honestly, I'm not too certain.”

“Hmph, don't worry about that too much, you did a good job today.” Once Mydei was done mothering Hyacine, he patted a hand on her rosy locks and grabbed Phainon’s wrist to tug him back to their corner and shove him in place. Then, like a king on his throne, Mydei sat on the man’s lap.

To add to the regal image, Phainon was even feeding him pomegranate seeds from a small platter, ignoring the beady eyes watching them. Ica was hungry.

Before she could think about what she was saying, too drained from the day and distracted with slipping on her bathing robe, Hyacine said, “Mydei, you shouldn't snack so late in the day, it can lead to more nausea and stomach discomfort.”

Normally, the man would be appreciative of her knowledge on aspects such as this – he treated his body like a temple and stayed away from keeping unhealthy habits, accentuating the importance of a good diet.

Out of the corner of her eye, Hyacine saw Phainon go pale, desperately waving a hand at her as if to tell her to stop. But it was too late.

“Actually, you look a little bloated. Should I give you a digestive tonic?”

Hyacine really didn’t mean to hurt his feelings. In the past, Mydei had always accepted them with a smile, or even asked for the tonics himself when his stomach was feeling off.

But it was like she had kicked a chimaera. For a moment, Mydei’s eyes widened, stunned, and then they were filled with tears as he warbled in a heartbroken voice, “Do I?”

“No, of course not, Dei, Hyacine’s just joking!” Phainon rushed to fix the damage, cuddling Mydei into his chest and hiding his face as he placed a conspicuous finger over his lips to tell Hyacine to be quiet.

She wasn’t joking about the bloating, but ok.

“Ahaha, Hyacine got whacked in the head by that titankin earlier, she's not in her right mind.” Castorice’s words were a betrayal, but Hyacine couldn’t find it in her to be mad at how she had her familiar notebook out, making notes. She really wondered what she wrote there. Then violet eyes were fixed on her, expecting her to do something to comfort the sniffling man in Phainon’s lap, and Hyacine panicked.

She did the first thing she could think of. She threw Ica at Mydei.

“Doot doot!” Mydei's pupils dilated as he watched the white blur sail towards him, and he caught Ica with one hand to cuddle up to them with a delighted noise.

The tears were gone, dried up in the prospect of being able to hold Ica (even as Phainon’s breath left him in a swift exhale as the weight on his lap drastically increased). Ica, however, only looked mournfully at the pomegranate seeds left on the platter beside them, unable to stretch out and steal them.

Hyacine finally slipped back into the bath to enjoy the peaceful silence that came with bathing so late in the day. Too exhausted from the day, no one said a word.  All she could hear was the rippling of golden water, Castorice’s steady breaths, and–

“Phainon, my chest hurts.”

She could only watch in despair as Castorice’s breath sped up, her posture becoming rapt with attention as Phainon gave an indulgent hum and started massaging Mydei’s chest with reverent hands.

While it was a well-known fact that Phainon and Mydei were relatively shameless when it came to skinship, it was surprising to see how… innocent Phainon’s touches were, focused solely on relieving pain.

He chuckled, his hands pressing down near Mydei’s sternum. “Honey, aren't you shy, admitting that in public like this?”

Ugh. Pet names.

Mydei blinked one eye open lazily. “Why should I be? I imagine Castorice is well-versed in matters such as these, and Hyacine already knows of my condition.” He shot her a knowing look, as if she were in on some secret that she had no idea about. “Besides, there’s nothing to be shy about; they're practically family.”

It was truly adorable how comfortable Mydei had become over the years, going so far as to see them all as family. While Hyacine, Castorice and Phainon had all at least shared their education in the Grove, bonding over last-minute essays and early-morning lectures, Mydei had spent his youth mostly in turmoil – be it drowning in the Sea of Souls, leading his detachment and plundering cities, or overthrowing his father.

Now, with the newfound peace on Amphoreus, there was finally time for them to relax and bond as a family.

But something Mydei said had struck a chord in Hyacine – his ‘condition’ that Hyacine supposedly already knew of, and Castorice had experience in.

To name the facts: Mydei had been tired lately, was snacking more, was behaving more protectively, was quick to get emotional and had a swell to his stomach. And Castorice, as the demigod of Thanatos, was not only capable of sensing death, but also life.

Hyacine’s eyes widened. She looked at Mydei. At the softness in his hips, his chest, his stomach. The curve to his belly, slight enough to be mistaken for bloating but unmistakably there.

Yet Hyacine had watched as Aglaea took him under her wing, dressing him in fine robes, teaching him the art of leadership and treating him to the city's delicacies; she may have been cursed to lose her humanity as the years went on, but there was no doubt that Phainon was as dear to her as a son.

She must be feeling like a proud parent, Hyacine mused, watching as the woman's hands trembled slightly as she handled the set of tiny clothes.

Castorice handed over a hand-knitted blanket, decorated with images of cats and dogs playing in a field of golden wheat and red flowers. It was a beautiful thing, clearly shown to have taken time and effort, and Hyacine smiled as Mydei's eyes became watery when he accepted it.

He couldn't hug her in his condition, not wanting to put the baby at risk even if his immortal body might provide some protection, so he hugged the blanket instead, holding it close as he valiantly held back tears.

For such a scary man, Mydei looked cute like this, heavy with his unborn baby and showered in soft presents, a painfully domestic sight.

Hyacine looked into the basket and pulled out the last few gifts. “Ah, these ones are from Professor Anaxa and Ica, and… Krateros, I think.”

Anaxa had sent a pack of the Grove's signature coffee, not caring to wrap it, but writing a note on the side that simply said, ‘Infants are a handful. Take care.’ Everyone pretended not to notice as Aglaea scoffed when Mydei read the note aloud, even if the coffee was tied in a familiar thread of gold.

From Krateros, a set of carved wooden warriors and a flagon of freshly pressed pomegranate juice – it seemed he had found a new hobby in juice making.

As for Ica… they had sent a heavy package, clumsily wrapped in white paper and the word ‘ICA’ scrawled on it in black ink. Hyacine stared at it blankly.

What. Ica didn’t have thumbs. How did Ica wrap this, and write their name on it as well.

Mydei didn’t seem to have the same questions, opening the package to reveal a platter of preserved fruits and candies, which Hyacine could recognise as being from Ica’s special stash. How sweet!

If there was anything she had learned in her years of being a physician, it was that the trick to lulling babies to sleep was either by singing to them softly, patting them rhymicallly, or showing them something repetitive to calm them down.

So, in the infrequent breaks she had between patients, Hyacine had made a mobile.

Attached to a curved glass ceiling, decorated with stars and constellations of the sky, were eight long threads, and on six of those threads were little trinkets: a golden butterfly, a chubby unicorn, a miniature dromas, a mischievous grey cat, a lilac dragon and a cluster of white flowers.

And above them, on the remaining two threads, were an intertwined set of chimaeras, ginger and white like the ones familiar to the Garden of Life, nuzzling each other lovingly with their tails interlinked.

Hyacine had taken Tribbie’s help to make a rotating mechanism, and when she switched it on in demonstration, the mobile began to spin slowly, glowing faintly as the trinkets and chimaeras waltzed under the domed sky.

Mydei let out a shaky breath, raising his fingers to run them through the threads of the mobile, and murmuring, “Hyacine–”

Then his face twisted.

“Ngh–” Mydei curled in over his stomach, grasping at it in distress as he let out a pained groan, the gifts discarded to the side.

Castorice started forward, only to hold herself back at the last second; everyone else, however, tried to crowd around him with worry evident on their faces. But Hyacine, well-versed in remaining calm under pressure and immediately switching into physician mode, kept them back.

“Mydei?” She asked, her voice clear and firm, “What’s wrong? Is it the baby?”

He jerked his head in a nod.

Hyacine took his hands in hers, allowing him to clutch at them instead of potentially hurting himself by pressing on his belly. “What does it feel like?”

“Like– like a really bad muscle cramp–” He gritted out, his brows furrowed, and his eyes squeezed shut.

“Ok, that’s probably a contraction.” It wasn’t uncommon to have contractions this close to Mydei’s due date, but it could be the sign of his labour starting. “Do you remember your breathing exercises? Can you do them for me?”

Steadily, Mydei did as he was told – two short breaths followed by one deep exhale – but his pain didn’t seem to alleviate.

“Is this an isolated contraction?”

“No… I've had… a few–”

“Mydei, you should have told me!” Hyacine chided, but she didn’t want to stress Mydei out by telling him off more. “When was your last one?”

“Dunno… just now,” He slurred out, swaying a little from where he was sitting. “But you said… you said– two more weeks–”

If Mydei was having frequent contractions, then it was clear – he was in labour. Hyacine turned to the others hovering anxiously over them, her gaze focused on Aglaea. “Lady Aglaea, could you please contact Phainon?”

Thankfully, she had sent one of her nymphs alongside the man, and so it wouldn’t be too difficult for her to let him know that his baby was on the way.

“Here, I’ll open a Century Gate,” Trinnon looked slightly queasy as she did so, her face pallid at the sight of Mydei in such evident pain, yet her hands stable as she went through the motions.

Along with Tribbie and Trianne, Hyacine helped Mydei to his feet, supporting his shaky form as he winced through his contractions. And then all of a sudden, Hyacine heard a wet noise, and looked down to see the bottom of Mydei's clothes damp.

His water had broken.

“Wh-what?” He clutched at his belly, sweat slipping down his face as he panted out a panicked groan. “Hyacine, it’s too early!”

The terror was obvious on his agonised face, his breathing erratic and the hand cradling his belly shaking. The other hand, wrapped around Hyacine's shoulder, was steady, as though her firm grip was enough to soothe him.

She gave him a reassuring smile as she led him through the Gate, saying, “No, it’s alright. Two weeks isn’t enough to be premature, your baby will be fine, I promise.”

“The baby is just excited to see you!” Trianne chirped, and perhaps it was the knowledge that the Tribios triplets were bearers of prophecies, or perhaps it was simply the assured confidence with which she spoke, but Mydei took a deep breath, blinked a few times, and then he was back to his normal calm.

The actual birthing itself was nothing out of the ordinary; despite Mydei's different parts, his body seemed to have reorganised itself to deliver the baby, and once his initial concerns had dissipated, Mydei’s indomitable perseverance returned.

And shortly after, the baby was born, squalling and mewling with the strongest lungs of the Kremnoans.

“Well done, Mydei! You were right, she’s a girl,” Hyacine wiped the infant off with a soft towel, cleaning off the blood and other fluids before carefully placing her in Mydei’s embrace. “Ten fingers and toes, and a full head of white hair.”

Mydei was yet to return to his full lucidity, dazed from the pain and panting heavily as though he had just fought in a particularly difficult battle. Well, Hyacine thought, technically he had been in a battle.

Still, at the feeling of his daughter in his arms, her crying quietened by being close to her mother, golden eyes squinted open and trailed along her tiny body. Then after a pause, he mumbled, “...She looks like Phainon.”

What.

In Hyacine's opinion, newborn babies looked like raisins, too small and wrinkly to notice any major features other than their hair, if they had any. But, perhaps it made sense. After all, she had seen Mydei spend so long tracing the contours and lines of Phainon's features with his eyes in their daily life, loving and fond, so he was bound to recognise them, even in a smaller form.

“Nine months in my womb… and she looks exactly like her papa.” Mydei's words were that of disbelief, but his expression betrayed his delight, and he lifted the baby to plant a kiss on the downy strands of white.

For a moment, the room was quiet.

Then the baby began to shriek and Mydei flinched, writhing in agony as he looked tearfully at Hyacine, his expression pinched in pain once more. “Shit! What’s going on–?”

If someone asked Ica what their least favourite food was, Ica would probably have to say panic. Ica hated the taste of panic.

Meanwhile, the other man, Anaxa, sat there serenely, studying a piece of… something, while completely ignoring Phainon's terror. Ica found Anaxa to be an odd person, but he treated Ica with respect and always offered them food, so he must not have been that bad.

Anaxa had enlisted the help of Phainon and Ica to excavate a set of ruins in Tretos, claiming that ‘the land that once birthed the infamous Tretos lion, must therefore be capable of birthing a mega-dromas.’ Or something along those lines. Ica had been a bit distracted.

Initially, Anaxa was uninterested and merely corrected him in a flat tone. “Anaxagoras.” But then he suddenly looked up in surprise, “Oh? Don't you always call me ‘professor’?”

“Sorry I'm acting abnormally because my wife is in labour, and I'm stuck on a dromas in the middle of nowhere!”

“We're not in the middle of nowhere.” A bored reply. “This is Tretos.”

They could only squeak in alarm as quivering arms wrapped around their plush white form, and Phainon began rocking back and forth while squishing Ica in his arms therapeutically. “Ica, can you get me there?” His normally bright blue eyes were crazed, large as plates as he muttered “You’re strong, right? You could fly me over,” he punctuated those words with a little shake.

Ica was just a unicorn. “Doot-doot.”

It was when Hyacine was peeling off her gloves after a successful labour and an easy delivery – heh, Phainon may have the title, but Hyacine was the true Deliverer – that Phainon finally showed up.

The doors of the medical bay burst open, one of them splintering at the force with which Phainon barged through looking absolutely dishevelled; his hair was windswept and his coat was ruffled, but most of all, his eyes were frantic with worry.

“Mydei! Where’s Mydei?! Is he–”

And then his gaze landed on the bed, and he went stock still.

There Mydei was, looking unnaturally good for someone who had just given birth; Hyacine had  helped change him out of his dirtied clothes, instead dressing him in a clean white robe, and he had a glow on his face as he smiled down at the not one, but two babies cradled in his arms.

Hyacine didn't need to have the gift of prophecy to foresee Phainon's reaction to the sight.

“D-dei…” He blubbered, the waterworks already starting as he stumbled over to the bed. For a moment, Hyacine's expectations were surpassed as he reached a shaky hand out to tuck a strand of blond hair away from Mydei's face and caressed his cheek.

Then he collapsed into a puddle on the floor, right on the pillow that Hyacine had set down in anticipation of this happening.

Phainon looked like an infatuated dog, kneeling beside the bed and raising his head onto the mattress to see their babies before breaking down in tears as he sobbed into the sheets.

“I was right.” Mydei finally spoke, triumphant as he said, “Our first was a girl.”

“Healthy… they’re– are they healthy?”

“Twenty fingers, twenty toes and two sets of white hair.” At that, Mydei looked happy, and surprisingly proud, “Both our babies are like mini-yous, except our son has my eyes.”

Hyacine thought it was quite funny how out of two babies and a freshly postpartum mother, Phainon was the one crying the most.

Phainon's tears lessened, and he sniffled as he got to his feet to sit on the chair beside the bed – Hyacine had placed it there, anticipating this as well – stretching his hand out to card his fingers through Mydei's hair lovingly.

“How… how are there two of them?” He asked as he looked down at the babies, their little faces scrunched up in sleep.

Honestly, Hyacine mainly had herself to blame for that. The scanner she had used was slightly outdated, resulting in a more blurry image, and upon seeing the babies in the womb, curled up closely together, she had just assumed that it was one abnormally large baby. It wasn't that far-fetched considering how tall the parents were.

But she wasn't going to tell them that.

“One of them must have been hiding behind the other in the early scans.”

Maybe that was a sign to finally go and ask the Grove to develop their technology further.

“They’re so small…” Phainon stroked a finger across a chubby cheek, his eyes watering once more.

They’re so fat, Hyacine thought, because even if there were two babies and not one monstrously sized one, the twins were rather plump for their age. And Hyacine was used to looking at Ica, so clearly– wait. Where was Ica?

“Phainon,” The serious tone with which Mydei spoke snapped both Phainon to attention, only for his next words to be, “let’s have more.”

A full quint hadn't even passed. Mydei's insides were likely still wounded – though, perhaps his unique body helped hasten his healing – and he looked close to passing out from exhaustion.

He looked better than Phainon at least. Phainon started wailing again. “No more… I can’t do this to you again, honey,” he warbled, and Hyacine found it sweet how he cuddled Mydei close with his words.

“But they’re so cute,” Mydei cooed, and poked their son's tiny cheek, causing the baby to snuffle, “they look just like you.”

Again. Hyacine frowned as she stared at the man in confusion. Newborns looked like raisins.

“Imagine taking them around Okhema… the shopkeepers would spoil them, for sure,” Mydei was grinning as he spoke, potentially delirious from the aftershocks of pain, but still boundlessly happy. “And we could show them the chimaeras, let them play together…”

At his words, Phainon perked up once more and reached into his pockets. “O-oh. Cipher gave me,” he paused his words to sniffle, “Cipher gave me her gifts.”

And he tucked two fuzzy plushies beside their babies, a lion and a dog. The movement woke their daughter, and blue eyes met blue as she squinted at Phainon.

“Hello, darling,” he crooned, leaning down to press a warm kiss to his daughter’s head, giving her a wobbly smile when she made a small affectionate noise in return.

Hyacine found it funny how the babies hadn't even been named yet. Maybe she should say so, and remind the new parents that no, they couldn't keep calling their babies ‘sunshine’ and ‘darling’ forever, but she had a feeling that they wouldn't hear her. They were too enraptured with their newborns, already wrapped around their delicate little fingers.

It was alright, Hyacine was used to fading into the background whenever Phainon and Mydei were together. Besides, with her luck, she probably wouldn't be away from their growing family for long.
